newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lawyers nationwide are set to contest seats in the Constitution-writing assembly as part of the Law Society of Thailand's ambitious bid to form a powerful voice in the upcoming political reform process. The society will field lawyers in all 76 provinces for the elections, which are to be held on Dec 15 and in which applicants in each province will select among themselves 10 "second-round" candidates. (THE NATION)

- The Police Department will not investigate the actions of Pol Gen Salang Bunnag in the Suphan Buri province massacre. Six men, said by police to be amphetamine traffickers, were handcuffed and led by a team of policemen headed by Salang into a house where they were shot. (BANGKOK POST)

- The prime minister used his first day in office yesterday to head off looming crises by promising to deal quickly with farmers' complaints and ordering a review of the Kaeng Sua Ten dam and Phu Kradeung cable car projects. In moving quickly, PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has tried to avoid pressure brought to bear by groups that converge on parliament to demand action on long-standing problems including expropriation and the state's failure to promote income-supplement programmes. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Premier and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has suggested that interest rates will be lowered to boost business liquidity and private investment amid an economic slowdown in which export growth is forecast to be zero for this year. He says an interest rate cut would be an immediate measure to heal the economic ills, which would be followed by longer-term measures such as government budget control, and tariff and industrial restructuring. (THE NATION)

- State-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) will buy electricity from the Union Energy-Tomen-IVO and Gulf Electric consortia under the first round of phase two of the Independent Power Producer (IPP) scheme. The total amount of power to be purchased from the two producers is 2,100 megawatts. (BUSINESS DAY)

- A major international maker and supplier of machinery for the paper, board and pulp industries will build its first technology centre in Asia in Chon Buri province. Valmet Corp of Finland will initially spend US$10 million to build the centre. It will be run by its subsidiary, Valmet Technology (Thailand) Co. (BANGKOK POST)
